veryMAD

MAD-based QC annotation and robust scaling for R

veryMAD flags selected numeric metrics with median absolute deviation (MAD) thresholds and scales numeric vectors, matrices, and data frames. You choose the metrics, directions, transformations, and filtering decisions.

[!IMPORTANT] A flag marks a statistical outlier in the supplied data. It does not diagnose low-quality cells or remove observations. Review metric definitions, distributions, and biological context before filtering.

Install 

pak::pak("Thokas99/veryMAD")

Annotate QC metrics

Rows are observations. Choose a tail for each metric; mad_qc() adds one logical flag per metric and a combined mad_qc_outlier flag.

Direction Flagged values
lower Below the lower threshold
upper Above the upper threshold
both Below or above the thresholds 
library(veryMAD)

metadata <- data.frame(
  nCount_RNA = c(820, 910, 970, 1050, 1120, 100),
  nFeature_RNA = c(430, 480, 520, 570, 610, 55),
  percent.mt = c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 35)
)

annotated <- mad_qc(
  metadata,
  metrics = c(nCount_RNA = "lower", nFeature_RNA = "lower",
              percent.mt = "upper"),
  transform = c(nCount_RNA = "log1p", nFeature_RNA = "log1p"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

annotated[, c("nCount_RNA_mad_outlier", "nFeature_RNA_mad_outlier",
              "percent.mt_mad_outlier", "mad_qc_outlier")]

Transformations are applied before threshold estimation. Count-like metrics often benefit from log1p; choose transformations and directions for the assay and protocol.

Inspect thresholds

Set output = "report" to return flags, thresholds, and settings without adding columns to the input.

report <- mad_qc(
  metadata,
  metrics = c(nCount_RNA = "lower", nFeature_RNA = "lower",
              percent.mt = "upper"),
  transform = c(nCount_RNA = "log1p", nFeature_RNA = "log1p"),
  output = "report",
  verbose = FALSE
)

report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "lower_raw", "upper_raw",
                      "status", "n_used", "n_flagged", "n_unresolved")]

n_used counts non-missing reference observations. The status and unresolved counts identify metrics or groups without usable thresholds; zero MADs produce unresolved flags by default.

For multi-sample data, pass one batch label per observation to batch to estimate thresholds within each sample. Use subset for an independently defined reference set; thresholds are still applied to every observation. Within-sample thresholds can miss a uniformly poor sample, so inspect distributions and consider separately justified absolute criteria. plot_mad_qc() shows each metric’s distribution by batch with flags highlighted. plot_mad_qc_scatter() shows paired metrics and reports within-batch Spearman rho and finite observation-pair counts. Pass a matching output = "report" result to add raw-scale cutoff lines. Correlations are descriptive; no p-values are calculated. Both plot functions require ggplot2.

For Seurat, QC metrics must already be present in cell metadata. For example, use a species-appropriate feature set and the intended RNA assay with Seurat’s PercentageFeatureSet() to calculate mitochondrial percentage. The function divides selected-feature counts by all counts in the chosen assay and reports 0–100%. veryMAD flags supplied metrics but does not calculate them.

Scale with MAD 

gene_expression <- c(gene_A = 8.2, gene_B = 8.7, gene_C = 18.0)
mad_scale(gene_expression)

Numeric data frames are returned as matrices; matrix dimensions and dimnames are preserved. For matrices and data frames, margin = 1 scales rows and margin = 2 scales columns. When scaling, zero_mad = "na" returns NA for zero-MAD groups. "zero" uses a unit denominator; centered results are deviations from the median. "error" stops.
